question.problem: Starting with the standard Maclaurin expansion for $\operatorname{cos}⁡x,$ find the first three non-zero terms of the series expansion for $\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}^{2})\,\text{d}x.$
question.worked_solution:
The series expansion of $\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ is

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡x=1-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2!}+\frac{{x}^{4}}{4!}+⋯\,.
$$

Replacing $x$ with ${x}^{2}$ in the above formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}^{2}) & =1-\frac{{({x}^{2})}^{2}}{2!}+\frac{{({x}^{2})}^{4}}{4!}+⋯\, \\  & =1-\frac{{x}^{4}}{2!}+\frac{{x}^{8}}{4!}+⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we multiply the series by $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}^{2}) & =x(1-\frac{{x}^{4}}{2!}+\frac{{x}^{8}}{4!}+…) \\  & =x-\frac{{x}^{5}}{2!}+\frac{{x}^{9}}{4!}+⋯\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, integrating with respect to $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}^{2})\,\text{d}x & =\int (x-\frac{{x}^{5}}{2!}+\frac{{x}^{9}}{4!}+⋯)\text{d}x \\  & =C+\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}-\frac{{x}^{6}}{6\cdot 2!}+\frac{{x}^{10}}{10\cdot 4!}+⋯ \\  & =C+\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}-\frac{{x}^{6}}{12}+\frac{{x}^{10}}{240}+⋯.\end{aligned}
$$
